result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.schema_ok]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: Whether the schema check passed. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.schema_ok]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: Whether the schema check passed. title: >- [Comparison.schema_ok]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Whether the schema check passed. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the schema check passed. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [Comparison.schema_ok]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} A comparison checks the two tables' schemas before it compares their values. How a schema difference is treated depends on `schema=` in [`compare()`](`pointblank.compare`). With `schema="strict"` (the default), `schema_ok` is the same as [`SchemaDiff.matches`](`pointblank.SchemaDiff.matches`), and a `False` value means that every test unit fails, so [`n_passed`](`pointblank.Comparison.n_passed`) is `0`. With `schema="common"`, schema differences are only reported, so `schema_ok` is always `True`. This makes `schema_ok` the property to check when a comparison fails and it's not clear whether the values or the columns are to blame. The details of the difference are in `schema_diff`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here, the target table has the same rows as the source, plus a new `humidity` column. ::: {#95abb808 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl readings = pl.DataFrame({"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3"], "temp": [12.1, 14.0, 9.8]}) readings_new = readings.with_columns(humidity=pl.Series([0.61, 0.58, 0.72])) comparison = pb.compare(readings, readings_new, keys="station") comparison.schema_ok, comparison.status_counts, comparison.n_passed ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (False, {'match': 3, 'changed': 0, 'missing': 0, 'extra': 0, 'dup_key': 0}, 0) ``` ::: ::: Every row has a status of `"match"`, but none of them pass, because the schema check failed. The cause is in the schema differences: ::: {#d3eb1669 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} comparison.schema_diff.only_in_target ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['humidity'] ``` ::: ::: If the new column is expected, `schema="common"` compares the shared columns and lets the rows pass: ::: {#8c369203 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} relaxed = pb.compare(readings, readings_new, keys="station", schema="common") relaxed.schema_ok, relaxed.n_passed ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (True, 3) ``` ::: ::: The new column is still listed in `relaxed.schema_diff`, so the change remains visible in the report even though it no longer fails the comparison.
